pr_title: drivers: flash: stm32h7: Data to write might not be nbytes aligned
pr_body:
Deal with the case of non-nbytes-aligned write input buffer.

Fixes #59029
pr_comments:
@erwango, if the read is unaligned it will never align and it would be needed to memcopy inside the loop. The simplest would be just to always do that.

BTW it is strange that an unaligned end is accepted, shouldn't this be errored out in the range check ?

I think this is a broader problem than just the stm32h7 driver. I am encountering the same on stm32u585xx and it's probably not just limited to those. Do we need to change each driver or is there a place we can make a broader change?

> I do not think this is correct fix.

Fully agreed

> NVS, where the problem occurs in reported isseu uses write alignment it reads from flash driver (write_block_size).
This means that NVS gets incorrect info on alignment
> Instead of fixing this by overwriting data several times, as I suspect happens here, correct write alignment should be reported for subsystems writing to the flash.

On this point, I'd be glad you were right, but this is set as:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/0773cc88c881bce51ae510ec150f03b69501e6d1/dts/arm/st/h7/stm32h7a3.dtsi#L18-L20
which is inline with ref man ([RM0455.pdf](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0455-stm32h7a37b3-and-stm32h7b0-value-line-advanced-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf)):
`Flash memory programming by 128 bits (user area) and 16 bits (OTP area)`

Am I missing something?

I think I am now missing what is happening. The problem is not that the flash operation is unaligned, the problem is that the data is unaligned.

The data that is passed to a flash operation should not be aligned, if the flash driver needs this to be aligned it has to do that itsself.

It should be possible to create a simple test that consist of creating a string that is twice the write-block-size, and then writing one wbs that starts at incrementing position. This should never fail, but i suspect it does.

The solution would be to use intermediate data buffer of `write_block_size`, beginning at required source alignment address.
So once you start with unaligned buffer, you copy each chunk through that buffer.
This way writing flash cells multiple time could be avoided, as long as users do correct math with `write_block_size`.
@Laczen thanks for clarification with https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/59098#issuecomment-1591781299.

Btw. I have looked at the `write_ndwords` and it seems that this is hardcoded to 8 byte alignment `write_block_size` :
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/e1efafa31db942f1a2557b967a22da522c4526ee/drivers/flash/flash_stm32h7x.c#L309-L310
as name suggests, so I guess that write block size 16, as this comments shows https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/59098#issuecomment-1591249334, seems ignored; copy is simply done by assignment:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/e1efafa31db942f1a2557b967a22da522c4526ee/drivers/flash/flash_stm32h7x.c#L344-L352

@erwango I have tested two of the possible solutions to this issue on STM32H7 series, so please take a look and see if any of these are worth implementing as a fix upstream:

- Use `memcpy` to copy the source data into temporary `write-block-size`-aligned buffer, and then write it to flash: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/compare/main...tmilkovic51:zephyr:fix-h7-unaligned-read-in-flash-driver
  - This approach adds an additional space overhead (write block size temporary buffer on stack) and processing overhead (extra `memcpy`-ing)
- Use `UNALIGNED_GET` macro to make compiler take care of unaligned read access to source buffer: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/compare/main...tmilkovic51:zephyr:fix-h7-unaligned-read-in-flash-driver-v2
  - This approach adds a slight performance penalty while accessing the source buffer (probably negligible compared to duration of flash write)
  - I'm also not sure if `UNALIGNED_GET` macro is available on non-GNU toolchains (it is defined in `gcc.h`) - other STM32 flash drivers use it (G0, L4 and WB), so compatibility with other toolchains could already be broken for these series


The same issue could also affect G4, L5, U5 and H5 flash drivers (I didn't check it on actual hardware, just inspected the code): 
- [G4](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/flash/flash_stm32g4x.c#L246)
- [L5/U5/H5](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/flash/flash_stm32l5x.c#L345)

> @erwango I have tested two of the possible solutions to this issue on STM32H7 series, so please take a look and see if any of these are worth implementing as a fix upstream:
> 
>     * Use `memcpy` to copy the source data into temporary `write-block-size`-aligned buffer, and then write it to flash: [main...tmilkovic51:zephyr:fix-h7-unaligned-read-in-flash-driver](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/compare/main...tmilkovic51:zephyr:fix-h7-unaligned-read-in-flash-driver)
>       

`memcpy` to intermediate is only needed for unaligned source. In all other cases you can just copy directly from source address. This would give you two paths of execution and increased flash size, but aligned wrights would be faster.

> > @erwango I have tested two of the possible solutions to this issue on STM32H7 series, so please take a look and see if any of these are worth implementing as a fix upstream:
> > ```
> > * Use `memcpy` to copy the source data into temporary `write-block-size`-aligned buffer, and then write it to flash: [main...tmilkovic51:zephyr:fix-h7-unaligned-read-in-flash-driver](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/compare/main...tmilkovic51:zephyr:fix-h7-unaligned-read-in-flash-driver)
> > ```
> 
> `memcpy` to intermediate is only needed for unaligned source. In all other cases you can just copy directly from source address. This would give you two paths of execution and increased flash size, but aligned wrights would be faster.

I would skip the trial to optimize and standardize on `UNALIGNED_GET()`, if compilers do not support it it should be added (it is also used in soc_flash_nrf.c). If on some devices it is not needed to do this the macro could be modified to do nothing (for that device).

>     * This approach adds an additional space overhead (write block size temporary buffer on stack) and processing overhead (extra `memcpy`-ing)

There is already a buffer for that called `unaligned_datas` so there is no additional space overhead. I don't think there will be a measurable overhead, given the flash write time is around ~5000 CPU cycles. IMHO it's best to keep the code simple (which also means smaller) and avoid too many code paths.

What `UNALIGNED_GET` basically does is read data, pointer by pointer, through intermediate variable of type the pointer provided to `UANLIGED_GET` is; so if you just go down to:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/e1efafa31db942f1a2557b967a22da522c4526ee/drivers/flash/flash_stm32h7x.c#L344-L352
And replace
```
flash[i] = data[i]; 
```
with:
```
uint64_t temp = data[i];
flash[i] = temp;
```
that should do the same thing, if `temp` gets aligned on stack to its type.

Thanks a lot guys for your time and attention on this point. Unfortunately, I've been busy with other topics.
I'll try to get back to this asap, but if needed don't hesitate to push new PRs and iterate. I wouldn't like to be the blocking point in this nice shared effort.

issue_context.title: subsys: lorawan: nvm: STM32H7 unaligned memory access (read) exception when writing LoRaWAN setting names to internal flash
comments: @tmilkovic51, probably something else is wrong, nvs should never do unaligned writes (when the write-block-size has been set correctly).

> @tmilkovic51, probably something else is wrong, nvs should never do unaligned writes (when the write-block-size has been set correctly).

Destination addresses for flash writes generated by NVS are fine. The issue here is, it seems, with misaligned reads of source data buffer (data which is to be written to flash). In this case, source data buffer is a misaligned Settings key value (string) located somewhere in `.rodata` section, which is mapped to MCU flash memory.
So, the setting key (unaligned string, in my case it was `"lorawan/nvm/MacGroup1"`) is being read from flash (`.rodata` section) by dereferencing an `uint64_t*` pointer, which generates an unaligned memory read from flash (I'm not an STM32/ARM expert, but maybe unaligned reads from RAM are fine, but it's unaligned reads from flash that generate the exception).

EDIT: Maybe the title of the issue was a bit misleading. I added to the title that read may be an issue

@tmilkovic51, the problem is IMO in the flash driver: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/flash/flash_stm32h7x.c#L374, this supposes that void *data is 8 byte aligned, which is not guaranteed.

@erwango fyi.
@tmilkovic51 I've followed @Laczen opinion and tried to deal with this case, please have a test: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/59098

> @tmilkovic51 I've followed @Laczen opinion and tried to deal with this case, please have a test: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/59098

Not fully ready yet. See my comments in PR

I think this is a broader problem than just the stm32h7 driver. I am encountering the same on stm32u585xx and it's probably not just limited to those. Do we need to change each driver or is there a place we can make a broader change?

@martincalsyn 
I've took a quick look at STM32 series flash drivers and this is their status (I didn't test it on actual hardware, just inspected the code):

- STM32F1, STM32F3, STM32L0, STM32L1 - uses `memcpy` to copy the source data into temporary (aligned) buffer (either `uint64_t`, `uint32_t` or `uint16_t`, depending on `write_block_size` property in flash controller device tree node)
- STM32F2, STM32F4, STM32F7 - uses byte-aligned read access while transferring source buffer to flash
- STM32G0 - uses `UNALIGNED_GET` macro to access the source data as `uint64_t`
- **STM32G4 - potentially same issue as STM32H7 - pointer to source buffer is directly casted to** `uint64_t*`
- **STM32H7 - as described in this issue**
- **STM32L5,STM32H5,STM32U5 - potentially the same issue as STM32H7 - pointer to source buffer is directly casted to** `uint64_t*`
- STM32L4, STM32WL - uses `UNALIGNED_GET` macro to acces the source data as `uint64_t`
- STM32WB - uses `UNALIGNED_GET` macro to access the source data as `uint64_t`

Series in bold could potentially have this issue. Affected files are: `flash_stm32h7x.c`, `flash_stm32l5x.c` and `flash_stm32g4x.c`. After unaligned read access is resolved in all of these, no series will be left affected.

Wow. All over the map. The UNALIGNED_GET seems like the least memory-expensive way to do it (though most cpu expensive). I have devkits here for all but the G4 series to test on. Do you plan to offer a revised PR or should I jump in in some fashion?

There are some solutions proposed in #59098, so take a look there. It's still TBD on what is the best way to resolve this, but good thing is that the same approach could be applied to all affected series if required.
